scope: Client combined statistics chart only. The production data source, filters, aggregations, rating distribution, reports, imports and synchronization are unchanged.

data_mapping.observations: series rows with count > 0, sorted by date; no fabricated buckets or values
data_mapping.label: series[].average formatted to one decimal in the account language
data_mapping.date: series[].date; detail shows the bucket interval clipped to the selected period
data_mapping.axes: Left: 1 to 5 stars. Right: zero to an adaptive integer maximum.
data_mapping.interaction: One local selection for the bar and point belonging to the same row. Touch, Enter/Space, Escape and close control; no API request when selecting.

screenshots.source: Synthetic test fixtures only, not production screenshots or real current restaurant totals. No mockup volumes or fallback datasets are embedded in the application.
screenshots.browser: Playwright Chromium with iPhone touch emulation (390 x 844); extra iPad check (820 x 1180). Physical iOS/Safari not tested.
screenshots.selection: All iPhone captures show the period, count and average after tapping a point. Both bar taps and point taps were exercised separately.

verification.scope: Combined chart, statistics navigation, history review list, translations, empty/error/loading states and existing report states.
Final CSS and screenshots after removing the browser's transient tap highlight.

assertions: Exactly one chart with one bar and one point per non-empty source row.
Bar center equals point x coordinate; sorted, equal spacing; continuous line painted above all bars.
Bar heights proportional to counts, count ticks integer and zero-based.
Unrounded point position verified with 10/3; label is 3.3 or 3,3 according to locale.
Empty state translated; single observation centered without line.
Touching either a bar or a point shows its own period/count/mean; keyboard access works.
Labels do not overlap; chart fits above fixed navigation when scrolled into view.
Sum of bar counts equals headline count and rating-distribution total in all three scenarios.
Additional actual RPC execution against isolated PostgreSQL: same totals for three months and 1,205 retained reviews with All selected.
Rating-distribution DOM unchanged when a chart observation is selected.
No extra network request is made by chart selection.
limitations: Mobile screenshots are emulations, not captures from a physical iPhone.
